corrections.why: The register gives 110 ft (33.5 m) for the current Aermotor. The record's 35.1 m equals 115 ft, the height newspapers gave for the 1913 wooden tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 121 ft for the original wooden tower and 110 ft for the current Aermotor. Newspapers of 1913 and 1921 give 115 to 116 ft for the wooden tower. The 110 ft figure is used for the standing structure.

notes_for_editor: Current access and rental status are not established by any source read; the only visit report on the register is from 2010. The record's point (34.36717, -111.01275) is about 1.4 km from the register's coordinates (N 34.377000, W 111.022250); not changed, a human should check which is right. The 1913 to 1952 history comes through newspaper quotations collected on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original newspapers. The LS-40 model name appears only on the Forest Lookouts page. The NRHP nomination PDF did not come through as readable text, so the nomination itself was not used. Height correction is proposed, not applied. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the first-tower sentence now cites both sources, and the 1921 to 1925 sentences are reworded to the sources. A March 1914 Albuquerque Herald item also credits C.H. Kissam, deputy forest supervisor, with building a 100-foot tower in the Sitgreaves forest; the story gives the credit to the 1921 Winslow Mail report and does not reconcile the two. The tower record at data/towers/az/us-az-promontory.json still shows height_m 35.1; the correction in this file's corrections array has not been applied there, so a human should decide it.
